Educational & Sporting Futures, also known as ESF Apprenticeships is a growing, innovative apprenticeship provider helping individuals aspire and achieve through education and training.

We're looking for someone organised, accurate and confident in communicating with different people.

- Experience in administration or a similar education / training administration role, ideally within apprenticeships.

- £29,000 - £32,000 salary depending on experience.

- The opportunity to develop within a dynamic and growing organisation.

Apprenticeships Administrator, Apprenticeship Coordinator, Apprenticeship Training Administrator, Compliance Administrator, Data & Compliance Assistant, Programme Support Officer, Training & Quality Administrator, Education Administrator, Talent Executive, HR Administrator or Recruitment Administrator with exposure to apprenticeships or funded training.

Ready to Be Part of Something Bigger?

At ESF Apprenticeships, you'll do more than help us onboard apprentices and manage our systems compliantly. You'll help unlock potential, shape futures and make a tangible difference in schools and communities nationwide.

If you're passionate about education, detail-driven and eager to grow with an award-winning apprenticeship provider, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Facilities Administrator
description:
Facilities Coordinator

27,000 + Annual Bonus & Reviews Hemel Hempstead Monday-Friday Office Based

Are you an organised, customer-focused coordinator with experience in Facilities Management, maintenance scheduling or a similar environment?

We're working with a growing and well-established business that is looking for a Facilities Coordinator to join their team, supporting a new project focussed on working with one of the largest and most recognisable companies in the world.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys being at the heart of things - coordinating engineers, speaking with clients, keeping jobs moving and making sure everything is organised and completed properly.

The company places a big emphasis on culture, teamwork and doing things the right way, so they're looking for someone who will fit into that environment just as much as someone with the right experience.

Please note that the offices for this role are based in a part of Hemel Hempstead with no public transport routes, so you must be a driver and have daily access to a vehicle.

What will you be doing?

You'll be responsible for coordinating a busy range of maintenance and facilities activity, acting as the main point of contact between clients, engineers and subcontractors.

Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating reactive maintenance, planned preventative maintenance (PPM), inspections and other scheduled works.
- Scheduling engineers and subcontractors, arranging access and keeping clients updated throughout the process.
- Speaking with engineers daily to provide job information, answer queries and make sure work is progressing as it should.
- Monitoring outstanding jobs and chasing reports, job sheets, timesheets and other information through to completion.
- Keeping job, scheduling and service information accurate across a number of systems.
- Maintaining trackers and purchase order logs, supporting the accurate monitoring of works, costs and invoicing.
- Supporting the financial administration of contracts, including checking subcontractor invoices and ensuring costs are accurate.
- Maintaining client compliance documentation and supporting wider quality and compliance requirements.
- Working closely with Operations, Engineering, Compliance and Finance to make sure everything runs smoothly.
- Assisting with reports, client reviews, audits and operational updates.
- Visiting client sites regularly to build relationships and keep up to date with what is happening on site.
- Looking for ways to improve processes, systems and the overall customer experience.

Don't worry if you haven't used all of the systems mentioned above - experience with scheduling systems or other facilities management software would be a big advantage, but we're more interested in someone who is organised, capable and picks things up quickly.

What are we looking for?

We're ideally looking for someone with at least some form of office based experience, anything relevant to FM or Scheduling is ideal but character is of the upmost importance to this company and they can train on a lot of the job.

You'll need to be:
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail.
- Comfortable working at pace and managing multiple priorities.
- Confident communicating with clients, engineers and subcontractors.
- Naturally proactive - someone who sees something that needs doing and gets on with it.
- Customer-focused and keen to build strong working relationships.
- Comfortable using Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Someone who enjoys being part of a team and contributes positively to the wider culture.

Please note: This is an office-based role, so you'll need to be able to drive and have access to your own vehicle, as there will also be visits to client sites.

What's on offer?
- 27,000 basic salary
- Discretionary annual bonus
- Full annual performance appraisal
- Monday-Thursday: 8:30am-5:00pm
- Friday: 8:30am-4:30pm
- Office-based role with regular client site visits
- Opportunity to work closely with a major aviation client
- A genuinely collaborative and culture-focused working environment
- The chance to develop your Facilities Management and coordination experience within an established business

title: Team Administrator
company: Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
description: Please be aware that this role is NOT eligible for Sponsorship If you already work for HPFT on a health and care visa, you will NOT be able to transfer your visa to this role as this role is NOT eligible for Sponsorship We are looking for a motivated, organised and welcoming Team Administrator to join our Adult Community Division This is a Band 3 role based across The Marlowes, Hemel Hempstead and 99 Waverley Road, St Albans, supporting staff across and working closely with the wider administration team to provide a consistent, efficient and responsive service. This is a varied role where no two days are the same. The successful candidate will provide a wide range of administrative support, including safeguarding, telephone cover, managing enquiries, booking rooms and appointments, supporting meetings with note taking , maintaining records and ensuring information systems are kept up to date. This includes using online systems such as Datix and Paris - Electronic Patient records. We are looking for someone who is professional, kind, positive and respectful, with good communication skills and the ability to organise and prioritise their own workload. The post holder will play an important part in supporting the smooth running of the service and contributing to a positive experience for service users, carers, visitors and colleagues. The post holder will provide high-quality administrative support to the team, working closely with colleagues across the service to ensure day-to-day tasks are completed effectively and in a timely way. Duties will include working on safeguarding for the team , answering and redirecting telephone calls, taking messages, greeting visitors, dealing with enquiries and supporting the smooth running of admin. The role will involve managing mail, booking rooms, preparing and arranging meetings (including safeguarding ) and appointments, updating diaries, supporting staff training bookings and completing general administrative tasks such as photocopying, scanning, emailing, archiving, typing and filing. The successful candidate will also support safeguarding and the maintenance of accurate records and information systems, including patient administration systems, and will be expected to handle information safely and confidentially in line with Trust policies. The post holder may be required to take minutes on occasion, chase actions and outcomes, organise patient transport and support the team with routine communication relating to appointments, admissions, discharges and transfers. The Team Administrator will provide a reliable and flexible administrative service to staff based across two locations. The post holder will work as part of the wider administration team and will support Senior Team Administrators, Assistant Team Administrators, Receptionists and Medical Secretaries to deliver a consistent and effective service. The successful candidate will be expected to manage their own workload, work without direct supervision at times, use initiative within agreed procedures and recognise what needs to be prioritised. The role requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to respond calmly and professionally to competing demands. The post holder will complete a range of administrative tasks including typing, note / minute taking , filing, scanning, photocopying, archiving, email correspondence, booking appointments, arranging meetings, updating diaries, supporting bring-forward systems and maintaining both paper and electronic filing systems. The role will involve maintaining accurate service user information on electronic systems, supporting appointment changes and cancellations. The post holder will communicate regularly with service users, carers, colleagues and external agencies. This will require a friendly and professional approach, including the ability to provide and receive routine information with tact and sensitivity, particularly where people may be anxious, distressed or experiencing communication barriers. Although the role has no clinical responsibility, the post holder will contribute to service user care by supporting administrative processes linked to appointments, clinics, admissions, discharges and patient transport. The successful candidate will also be expected to support new or less experienced staff by demonstrating departmental procedures, offering advice about their own role and providing mentorship to lower banded staff where appropriate. Applicants should have experience of working in an office environment, good keyboard and telephone skills, confidence using Microsoft Word and email, and the ability to organise, prioritise and complete work accurately. A friendly manner, calm approach, good communication skills and a professional attitude are essential. The post would suit someone who works well as part of a team, can manage interruptions and changing priorities, and is committed to supporting high-quality care through effective administration. Car driver essential as a majority of the posts are community based, the post holder will need a full valid driving licence and access to a car to use regularly for business purposes including business insurance (unless you have a disability as defined by the Equality Act 2010).

title: Administrator
description: Larksfield and Arlesey Medical Partnership is seeking a motivated and organised Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team. This is a varied role that provides essential administrative support across the practice, helping to ensure the efficient day-to-day running of services and supporting the delivery of safe, high-quality patient care. Working closely with the management team, clinicians and colleagues, you will contribute to a range of administrative functions while maintaining professionalism, confidentiality and excellent customer service he successful candidate will support safeguarding administration, manage incoming and outgoing correspondence, prepare meeting agendas and minutes, maintain safeguarding registers and action logs, and respond to administrative queries. The role also includes supporting the Rota Manager with clinician rota coordination, maintaining accurate records and clinical rotas, producing reports and documentation, and assisting with governance, quality improvement and CQC compliance activities. You may also provide administrative support to the reception and secretarial teams during periods of operational demand. Provide comprehensive administrative support across the practice. Support safeguarding administration, including maintaining safeguarding registers, trackers and action logs. Process safeguarding correspondence, referrals and information requests. Prepare meeting agendas, take accurate minutes and circulate actions. Monitor shared email inboxes and ensure correspondence is actioned appropriately. Respond professionally to administrative queries from patients, staff and external organisations. Escalate urgent clinical, safeguarding or operational concerns where appropriate. Support the Rota Manager with booking locum clinicians and maintaining clinical rotas. Ensure clinician sessions and rota changes are accurately recorded and communicated. Maintain accurate electronic records, spreadsheets and filing systems. Produce reports, letters and other administrative documentation. Support audits, searches and governance activities, including CQC evidence gathering. Work collaboratively with clinicians, reception, secretarial teams and external stakeholders. Maintain confidentiality and comply with all practice policies, information governance and safeguarding procedures. Provide additional administrative support across departments during periods of increased operational demand.

title: Coordination Centre Administrator
description: Coordination Centre Administrator Hours: 37.5 hours per week Location: Peace Hospice, Watford Salary: £25,446 per annum (pro rata) Closing date: 3 September 2026 at 12 noon Interview date: TBC What you will do: Acting as the first point of contact for patients, families and professionals and provide a kind and knowledgeable response when dealing with callers and knowing how and when to escalate. To deal appropriately and sensitively with all callers, adhering to hospice policies on confidentiality at all times. Working collaboratively with others in the Coordination Centre, including clinical colleagues and support them to ensure the patient and family receive the appropriate care in a timely way. Ensuring that data entry on to the clinical systems is complete and accurate. Work on a rota basis covering 8am to 6pm, seven days a week. --Shifts could be: Earlies: 8am - 4pm Day: 9am - 5pm Late: 10am - 6pm Acting as a Rennie Grove Peace Hospice Care ambassador Management of all referrals into Rennie Grove Peace, both those from external sources and internal referrals. Ensure that the correct team is notified of the referral and the priority score in order that the patient and family receive care in a timely fashion. Ensure that the correct data is entered into the clinical system. Call patients and family members to arrange appointments. Take messages from professionals, patients and family members to ensure they are passed to the most appropriate person. Pull data from the clinical system for pre-planned reports such as patient lists or missing data reports. Book rooms for appointments, prepare clinic letters and process patient discharge summaries, ensuring these are all completed in a timely manner. Support and train those new to the team including volunteers. To work with the SystmOne (S1) champions across the hospice, being able to provide the S1 admin induction sessions for all new staff and contribute to the S1 train the trainer sessions. Lead others across the organisation by acting in a professional, kind and competent manner at all times.

title: Administrator - Hertfordshire
description: Job summary Job title: Administrator Contract: Bank Start: September 2026 until December 2026 Working Hours: Monday to Friday between 8:00am - 5:00pm. (7.5 hour shift per day) BENEFITS: Pension - 5% employer contribution based on qualified earnings. VIVUP - Supermarket & High Street Discounts & Employee Assistant Programme. Blue Light Card - Supermarket & High Street Discounts. Employee referral scheme. 28 days annual leave including Bank Holidays (pro-rata). Main duties of the job The post holder will be responsible for promoting, delivering, and facilitating various programmes directed by management as part of the School-Aged Immunisation Service assisting nurses in the schools or office. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: Assist in the planning, delivery and evaluation of health promotion/education and public health school age immunisation programmes. Attend community-based vaccination sessions in both schools and local based settings. Work with the nursing team to ensure productive and safe sessions. Promote and facilitate collaborative working between the team, schools and other educational institutions and families, in the delivery of the immunisation programmes. Focus on ensuring all consent forms have been returned, guaranteeing new ideas go towards achieving local area targets. Ensure the process for storing, transporting, collecting and delivering vaccinations to site are adhered to. Assist in identifying home schooled children and those in Pupil Referral Units. Maintain databases to ensure records are kept up to date and that documents are prepared for school visits. Ensure online consent systems have been triaged and completed ahead of a vaccination session. Adhere to the Standard Operating Procedure for School Immunisation (SOPs). First point of contact for all administrative tasks. Have clear communication via face to face, by phone and email with children, parents and school staff. Responsible for maintaining the cold chain, ordering, and arranging transport of vaccinations to site. Actively and constructively contribute to team meetings. Undertake other duties commensurate with the level of this position. Comply with Company policies & procedures.
